cases.question: Among schools with a school-level SAT excellence rate above 0.3, what is the highest ages-5-17 free-meal eligibility rate?
cases.evidence: SAT excellence rate is the share of test takers scoring at least 1500.

cases.question: For locally funded schools whose K-12 minus ages-5-17 enrollment difference exceeds the average such difference among locally funded schools, list each school's directory-listed name and DOC type.
For the five schools with ownership code 66 and the largest K-12 free-or-reduced-price meal counts, give each school's K-12 eligible meal rate rounded to six decimal places.

What is the lowest grade level at which any school in our district begins serving students? If several schools tie at the lowest grade, just report that single grade level for the whole district. Our district is NCES district ID 0632640.
cases.evidence: 'P' stands for preschool.

cases.question: I'm planning reviews of Provision 2 meal programs under the NSLP and want to see which cities concentrate magnet schools under that provision. For each city that has at least one, can you give me the number of the city's magnet schools that run a Provision 2 meal program? Use the city where the school is located, not its mailing city. Also, if a school's NSLP entry lists multiple provision types, don't count it as running Provision 2.
cases.evidence: NSLP is the National School Lunch Program. Provision 2 is a federal provision under the NSLP that lets a school serve meals at no charge to all students regardless of family income.

cases.question: What rules text is printed on Benalish Knight? Return the distinct text as one line.
Among the sets in the block "Ice Age", how many of them have an Italian translation?
I collect promotional printings and play Brawl. How many different creature cards that have a promotional printing can serve as a Brawl commander? I just want a single number back.
cases.evidence: A promotional printing is a printing of a card made as a promotion, as opposed to a regular set printing. Brawl is a Magic: The Gathering format; the deck's commander is the card that leads it, and only certain cards are legal as a Brawl commander.

cases.question: I'm putting together a showcase of zero-mana-cost cards. What is the newest frame version used by any card with a converted mana cost of 0? Please give me that frame version value, and the number of cards in the database that use that frame version. The count should cover all cards in the database, not just the zero-cost ones. If several frame versions tie as the newest, give me each of them with its own count.
cases.evidence: Frame version: the edition of the card frame style a printing uses.

cases.question: I'm tracking John Avon's artwork. Among his cards that exist as powerful foils, what is the most recent frame year, and how many of those cards carry it? If several years are tied for most recent, give each year with its own count. Match John Avon on the illustrator's name.
cases.evidence: powerful foil: a card whose Card Kingdom identifiers are both present – the regular identifier and the foil identifier.

cases.question: Among the cards carrying the boros watermark that were printed in a foreign language, which card type is the most common, and how many of those cards have that type? If several types tie for the most, list all of them with their counts.
cases.evidence: "Boros watermark" refers to the guild watermark appearing on cards of the Boros guild; "printed in a foreign language" means the card was printed in any language other than English.

cases.question: Among the Magic: The Gathering cards whose watermark is one of the ten Ravnica guild symbols (Azorius, Boros, Dimir, Golgari, Gruul, Izzet, Orzhov, Rakdos, Selesnya, Simic), which guild has the most cards that were printed in another language, and how many of that guild's cards is that? If several guilds tie for the most, give me each tied guild along with the number.
cases.evidence: A Ravnica guild is the guild a card's watermark belongs to; a card 'printed in another language' is a card that exists in a language edition other than English.

cases.question: I'm assembling a Japanese-language boros deck and want to check which cards need careful rules review. For every card that has a boros watermark and a Japanese printing, please give me: the Japanese card name, the English card type, and the total number of official rulings recorded for that card. A card is identified by its Japanese name together with its English card type - printings that share both count as one card, and if either differs they should be listed as separate cards. The ruling total should add up all ruling entries across every printing of that card, and if a card has no rulings, list it with a total of 0.
cases.evidence: Boros watermark means the watermark is marked 'boros' on the card; a Japanese printing is the foreign data entry in Japanese; rulings are the official rules clarifications recorded for a card.

cases.question: For a stats segment on creature power creep, I want to size the middle-to-big power band: how many card printings have a power greater than 3 and at most 10? Note that 3 itself is out (strictly greater than 3), but 10 itself counts (at most 10). Just the total number of printings, please.
cases.evidence: A printing is one printed appearance of a card in a set – the same card name appearing in different sets counts as several printings.

cases.question: Among the Commander-type expansion sets released in calendar year 2020 (1 January 2020 to 31 December 2020), I need the one with the highest total card count, so we can plan translation work. Please send me the set's id from the sets listing, its name, and the number of official languages it was released in. The total card count should include promotional and related supplemental products, but exclude Alchemy modifications. If two sets tie for the highest total card count, list each of them, ordered by set id ascending.
cases.evidence: Commander: a multiplayer expansion type of the game. Alchemy modifications: online-only variant versions of cards.

cases.question: What is the difference in percentage points between the 2010 and 2011 shares of all Student badges, taking the 2010 share minus the 2011 share?

I'd like to gauge the standing of our United Kingdom contributor community on the site. Can you give me the combined reputation of the users based in the United Kingdom who have posted on the site, as a single total? Please write the country by its full name, "United Kingdom", and don't substitute abbreviations. I just need the one number, not a per-user list.
cases.evidence: Reputation is the score the site assigns each user. A user who has posted owns at least one item in the site's post collection.

cases.question: I'm profiling how seasoned our Organizer badge holders in Germany are. Among the users who earned the Organizer badge and are based in Germany, how many had already earned 5 badges before they got the Organizer badge? Just the count, please. Note: "before" means strictly earlier - badges earned at the same moment as the Organizer badge don't count toward the 5, and the Organizer badge itself doesn't count as one of the 5.
cases.evidence: Organizer badge: the badge whose name is Organizer.

cases.question: I'm putting together the yearly activity report with a Germany-focused breakdown of who did the editing, covering posts created in calendar year 2012. For the 2012 posts whose last editor is a user based in Germany, I need the total score; and for all other posts created in 2012, I need their total score as well. Also, how many Germany-based users were the last editor of at least one 2012 post, and what their combined reputation is, as shown on their profiles. A user based in Germany is one whose profile location is in Germany.
cases.evidence: A post's last editor is the user who made its most recent edit.

cases.question: Among all posts whose title contains the phrase 'principal component scores', which one has the most related posts linked to it? For each such post, give me the post title and the number of related posts. If several posts tie for the most, list every one of them with their counts. The count should cover related posts across the site's entire history.
cases.evidence: A related post is another post that the community's link records connect to a given post.

cases.question: I'm auditing accounts on the stats forum. What is the id of the youngest user account whose display name is Michael? If two or more such accounts tie as the youngest, give me the smallest id.

I'm reviewing 2013 uptake and want to know the genuinely active cardholder base in each client segment. For each client segment, how many of that segment's customers consumed any fuel at all during the calendar year 2013? I just need the client segment and the number of customers who consumed fuel in 2013, nothing else.
cases.evidence: A customer's consumption for a month is the amount of fuel recorded against them for that month; by 'consumed any fuel in 2013' I mean they had fuel recorded against them in at least one month of 2013.

cases.question: I'm preparing a loyalty review of our steadily active customers in 2013. For each currency, I'd like to know how many customers bought fuel in every month from January through November 2013, with both January and November included. Please give me the currency and that customer count. If several currencies tie, list them all – no ranking needed.
cases.evidence: Consumption means the total fuel a customer purchased in a month on their fuel card; a customer counts for a month if they had any consumption that month.

cases.question: I'm putting together currency-specific pricing proposals and need a sense of typical quarterly fuel consumption. Among customers who have fuel consumption recorded in the second quarter of 2013 (April, May and June 2013), what is the average amount of fuel consumed over the whole quarter by an EUR-paying customer, and the same average for a CZK-paying customer? Please round both averages to two decimal places. By EUR-paying / CZK-paying I mean a customer whose account currency is EUR / CZK.
cases.evidence: EUR-paying / CZK-paying: a customer whose account currency is EUR / CZK

cases.question: List the ten players taller than 180 cm with the highest mean recorded heading accuracy, highest first. Break mean ties by player API ID.
On what date did Kevin Constant first record his highest crossing score?

As part of a data-quality review for a segment report, I need to know how much of the recorded transaction activity for one of our segments has no payment purpose noted. How many transactions are there, over the whole recorded history, on the accounts held by male customers born between 1974 and 1976 (birth years 1974, 1975 and 1976), for which no payment purpose is noted? Please give me just that single number.
cases.evidence: Payment purpose: the stated reason or note recorded for a transaction.

cases.question: I'm preparing a partner-bank negotiation and want to focus on our big-city clients. Please tell me, for 1998 (1 January through 31 December 1998), where the money went from gold credit card clients' accounts held at branches in large districts. Specifically: for accounts whose owner has a gold credit card, and whose branch is located in a district with at least 250,000 inhabitants, look at their outgoing payments (debit transactions, type VYDAJ). I need a ranking of the recipient bank and counter-account pairs by the total amount paid. If two pairs tie for the largest total, list both. For each pair, give me: the recipient bank code, the recipient counter-account number, the number of outgoing payments, and the total amount paid.
cases.evidence: Gold credit card means card type 'gold'; account owner means disposition type 'OWNER'; the counter-account is the partner account at another bank to which a payment is sent; the district is the one where the account's branch is located.

cases.question: I'm putting together a review of our first credit card wave and need a profile of every client who was issued a credit card in 1994 (issue date falling in calendar year 1994). For each such client, please include: client id, gender, birth date, card type, age at card issue (the card's issue year minus the client's birth year), number of loans on their account, total amount borrowed, borrower classification, district name, district average salary, and their age rank within gender. Use these classifications: Young borrower if there's at least one loan on the account and age at card issue is under 30; Mature borrower if there's at least one loan and age at card issue is 30 or more; otherwise Non-borrower. The age rank within gender should be a standard competition rank - equal ages share a rank and the next rank is skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). Order the rows by client id.

I'm reviewing branches in the north Moravia region ahead of a client meeting. For each branch there, how many transactions dated on or before 14 October 1998 have no characterization recorded? A branch is the district the account belongs to, and the count should cover all of the branch's accounts' transactions. Please list only the top three branches by this count, with the branch name and its count, ranked first to third. If any branches tie on the count, order them alphabetically by branch name and keep three rows after that ordering.
cases.evidence: A transaction with no characterization recorded means the bank did not tag it with any characterization.

cases.question: I need to find out where our pre-1997 long-term mortgage exposure is concentrated geographically. Long-term means a loan duration of more than 24 months, and "opened before 1997" should exclude anything opened during 1997. Please tell me: for each region, which districts have at least one such account, and give me the region whose qualifying districts have the largest combined number of inhabitants. Along with the region's name, I want the number of those districts in it, their combined population, and the total number of those accounts in the region. If two regions tie on combined population, pick the one whose name comes first alphabetically.

For each year before 1975 with recorded winner times, what was the mean race winner elapsed time in seconds? Round the exact mean to two decimal places; if it is exactly halfway, round away from zero. Order by year.

Who won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix? I'd like the winner's forename and surname, the local clock time (hours:minutes:seconds.milliseconds) at the circuit at which he crossed the finish line, and the url of his information page, so I can compare the moment the race ended with the TV coverage.
cases.evidence: A driver's race time is the duration from the start of the race to the moment he crosses the finish line.

cases.question: I'm writing a piece about how the same common forenames recur across Formula 1 history. Could you tell me how many different drivers named Peter have ever won a Formula 1 race, and the same for drivers named John? Please give me one count per forename, so I can compare the two — if they turn out to be equal, just report both counts side by side. Nothing else needed.
cases.evidence: A race win means the driver finished first in that race.

cases.question: Across all seasons in the database, which circuit's Grand Prix started earliest in the day, and which started latest? I'd like the circuit reference name of the earliest one, the circuit reference name of the latest one, and the gap between those two start times in seconds. Include every season, and if several circuits share the earliest start time, list them all - same for the latest.
cases.evidence: By "start time of the day" I mean the local clock time at the venue at which the race started.

cases.question: For the 1957 British Grand Prix, what percentage of the drivers who took part in the race were classified finishers, rounded to two decimals? By classified finisher I mean a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner. I just need the one percentage figure.
cases.evidence: classified finisher: a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner

cases.question: I'm reviewing our roster against the catalog and want to see how much of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences' coverage our members actually hold, department by department. For each department in that college, give me: the department's name, the majors it offers, the majors held by at least one of our members, and the average members per major it offers, rounded to two decimals. Membership is as currently listed in the member records, and count a department as belonging to the college when any of its majors sits in the college.
cases.evidence: College of Humanities and Social Sciences: one of the colleges that houses departments offering majors.

cases.question: What is the date of the Vice President's most recent expense on record, and what is the total cost of all expenses incurred on that date? Consider all expenses on record with no earlier cut-off, and give the total exactly as it appears in the records, without rounding.
cases.evidence: Vice President is a position of the Student Club.

cases.question: I'm putting together a recruitment report for the colleges and want to know which parts of the university our club's membership actually draws from. For every person on the roster-regardless of their position in the club-look at their major, and the college that houses the department offering that major. Which college or colleges do the most majors on our roster come from, and how many majors is that? If there's a tie at the top, give me every college tied at that count. Please list the colleges in alphabetical order by college name, and return just each college's name and its number of majors.
cases.evidence: Major: a field of study offered by a department housed in a college.

cases.question: For every event in the club's records, can you give me the event name, event date, total amount budgeted for the event, and the number of members who attended it? Please sort the list by event name, then by event date, both in ascending order.
I'm preparing the year-end audit of club spending. For each item Sacha Harrison bought with club money, I need the item name and how many times she bought it. Can you give me that list?
cases.evidence: By "item" I mean an individual thing named in a record of what money was spent for.

cases.question: I'm putting together the end-of-term spending review. Who bought the most different kinds of items in October or November 2019? Please give me that member's full name, how many different kinds of items they bought in those two months, and their total spending in dollars over the same period. If two members tie for the most kinds, list every tied member with their kind count and spending.
cases.evidence: An item is one of the individual things a purchase covered, such as a pizza or a bottle of water.

cases.question: I'm writing an article about heroes who fall outside the classic good-versus-evil divide. How many superheroes in the database have an alignment that is neither good nor bad? Please give me just that count. Note that this should cover all superheroes in the database.
cases.evidence: good: a superhero whose alignment is Good; bad: a superhero whose alignment is Bad; alignment: the moral category assigned to a superhero

cases.question: What is the average weight in kilograms of the DC Comics heroes whose eye colour is also shared by at least one Marvel Comics hero? Leave out any heroes whose weight is unknown, round the result to the nearest kilogram, and treat 'No Colour' as an eye colour like any other when matching between publishers. I just want that single number.

What is the average weight, in kg, of the heroes who belong to races in which no hero is female? Heroes whose weight is not recorded should not count toward the average. I just need that single value.
cases.evidence: female: the hero's gender is female

cases.question: I'm writing a piece about which real publishing companies have put out very tall heroes. How many publishers in the database have released at least one hero taller than 200 cm? Note that taller than 200 cm means strictly more than 200 cm, and it counts if even one of their heroes is that tall. I just need the number of publishers, nothing else.
cases.evidence: A hero's publisher being 'released' means the publisher the hero is attributed to in the database.

cases.question: For a licensing survey of non-DC heroic characters, I need a single total count of superheroes whose alignment is Good and who are not published by DC Comics. Just that one number, please.
cases.evidence: Good means the hero's alignment is Good; DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.

cases.question: I'm comparing superhero body weights to typical human weights for an article. What is the average weight in kilograms of superheroes published by DC Comics, rounded to one decimal place, and how many DC Comics superheroes is that average based on? Only superheroes with a known weight should count toward the average, so the count should be the number of superheroes it's based on. DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
What is the average weight in kg of the Female heroes in the database? Round it to two decimal places, and skip any heroes whose weight is unknown. I just need that single number.
cases.evidence: kg: kilograms

cases.question: I'm comparing how power-rich male and female heroes are. For all male heroes and all female heroes that have a documented real full name, what is the average number of superpowers per hero for each gender? Please compute each average over the entire hero population of that gender, not just the heroes that happen to have power records. Give me both averages, each rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
cases.evidence: Full name: the hero's real, full personal name (first name plus last name, and optionally middle names); single names such as mononyms or aliases are not a full name.

cases.question: I'm doing a physical-profile breakdown of the George Lucas catalogue. For the heroes published by George Lucas that have at least one superpower in the database, what is their average weight in kilograms, counting only the heroes whose weight is recorded? Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: George Lucas refers to the publisher name.

cases.question: For the article I'm writing on heroic female characters, I'd like a physique stat for the trivia box: what is the average weight in kilograms of female superheroes whose alignment is good? Only count superheroes whose weight is known. Please round the result to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: Alignment: the superhero's moral category, e.g. good, bad, neutral.

cases.question: I'm preparing a report on Marvel's roster and want to gauge how heroic their catalogued heroes are. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose civilian full name is documented, what percentage are good? Please give me just that single percentage, rounded to two decimal places. Note: the percentage should be taken over all Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name - those whose moral alignment is unknown still count toward the total, just not as good.
cases.evidence: Good refers to alignment = 'Good'. A full name means the hero's real-world civilian identity, i.e. an actual person's name such as 'Charles Chandler' or 'Richard Milhouse Jones'.

cases.question: Among superheroes whose weight is not recorded, how many more have the 'No Colour' eye category than have blue eyes? I want a single whole number: the count of 'No Colour' eyes minus the count of blue eyes in that group - it can be negative if blue is more common. Please give me just that one number, with no other results or breakdowns.
cases.evidence: 'No Colour' is an eye category meaning the hero's eye colour is unspecified.

cases.question: How many distinct patients with a triglyceride result of at least 200 were older than 50 on 2026-10-09?
Among patients older than 55 on 2026-10-09 who have at least one abnormal PT result, what percentage are female? Round to two decimals.
cases.evidence: For this task, PT of at least 14 is abnormal.

cases.question: Among patients followed at the outpatient clinic who ever had an abnormal anti-SSA result, which one showed the highest anti-RNP titer? Please give me the patient's ID and the anti-RNP titer value. This should cover the hospital's full records across all years, and if several patients tie for the highest anti-RNP titer, list every one of them.
cases.evidence: Abnormal anti-SSA means any SSA result other than negative or 0. "Followed at the outpatient clinic" is the admission status marked with a minus sign. Anti-RNP titer is the strength of the anti-ribonuclear protein result.

cases.question: Among the thrombosis registry patients followed at the outpatient clinic, how many have a non-normal hematocrit and an anti-ribonuclear protein measurement above 16? I need a single count. A patient counts if they have at least one hematocrit reading outside the normal range, regardless of test date, and at least one anti-ribonuclear protein reading above 16, regardless of test date. Include every patient in the registry, not only those with a recorded thrombosis event.
cases.evidence: Hematocrit is normal when the value lies strictly between 29 and 52; outside that range it is abnormal. A negative anti-ribonuclear protein result means none was detected.

cases.question: I'm studying patients who carry exactly the rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome overlap. Please look at each patient's own record and find those whose record names exactly rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome, in either order, and no other disease – a disease recorded only as suspected does not count as a diagnosis. For those patients, considering their whole recorded laboratory history regardless of date, I need two numbers: how many have had at least one laboratory result showing a normal platelet level, and how many have never had a laboratory result showing a normal platelet level – count a patient with no laboratory results at all as never having had a normal platelet result.
cases.evidence: Rheumatoid arthritis is recorded as the code RA and Sjögren's syndrome as the code SJS. A normal platelet level means a platelet count above 100 and below 400.

cases.question: Among patients whose first visit to the hospital was in 1991, which patients mounted the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) response? Please give me the patient ID and anti-RNP level for every patient tied at the highest recorded level. Only consider patients for whom a level was actually recorded.
cases.evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody titer; a higher titer means a higher level.

cases.question: I'm reviewing confirmed SLE cases for a study of neurologic involvement. Among patients whose examination lists SLE among the diagnosed diseases and who have a symptom recorded at such an examination, I need the case detail of the youngest such patient. Please send me the symptom recorded at that qualifying examination and that patient's overall diagnosis (their overall diagnosis, not the diagnosis written at the examination). If two patients share the same birth date, use the one with the smaller patient ID; and if that patient has more than one qualifying examination, use the most recent one.
cases.evidence: SLE is systemic lupus erythematosus. A disease name followed by 'susp' means the disease was only suspected, not diagnosed.

cases.question: I need to size a comparison group for my study of liver-enzyme abnormalities. How many patients in the registry have never had an ALT result above the normal range? Please give me the count broken down by sex: the number of male patients and the number of female patients. Every patient in the registry counts, including patients with no laboratory results at all, since they have never had an abnormal result. The report should cover exactly the two sexes, male and female.
cases.evidence: ALT is measured by the GPT laboratory value; a GPT result of 60 or higher exceeds the normal range.

cases.question: For the carcinogenic molecules in the toxicology database, how many carbon-carbon bonds are there of each bond type (single, double, and triple)? Please give me the bond type and the corresponding count.
cases.evidence: A molecule labelled '+' is carcinogenic. Bond types are recorded as follows: a single bond as '-', a double bond as '=', and a triple bond as '#'. A carbon-carbon bond is a bond whose two bonded atoms are both carbon.

cases.question: I'm studying bond patterns in compounds that are not carcinogenic. For each element, how many double or triple bonds join a carbon atom to an atom of that element, across all non-carcinogenic molecules? Give me one row per element with the element and its count of such bonds—nothing else.
cases.evidence: A molecule labeled '-' is not carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic.
